title: Micromagnetic Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Normal-Mode Formulation of Cavity Magnon-Photon Interactions
authors: Claudio Serpico, Marco Lembo, Giovanni Miano
abstract: We investigate magnon-photon interactions in a resonant cavity starting from the coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations linearized about an arbitrary micromagnetic ground state. By introducing an electric vector potential and a suitable interaction Lagrangian, the formulation avoids the cancellation of large magnetostatic contributions that arises in the conventional magnetic-vector-potential description and becomes inaccurate under modal truncation. The magnetization and cavity fields are expanded in the normal modes of the uncoupled magnetic and electromagnetic subsystems, with coupling coefficients given by overlap integrals of the corresponding eigenfunctions. The resulting multimode Lagrangian has a noncanonical structure due to the gyrotropic terms, and the corresponding Hamiltonian formulation is obtained using the Faddeev-Jackiw approach. The radiative magnon-photon interaction is encoded in the resulting Poisson-bracket structure, while the cavity-induced modification of the magnetostatic field enters explicitly in the Hamiltonian. The coupled system is diagonalized through a generalized Bogoliubov transformation, yielding canonical polariton variables that provide a natural basis for quantization. Application to a perpendicularly magnetized YIG disk in a rectangular microwave cavity shows hybridization between the cavity mode and several magnetostatic modes, together with appreciable cavity-wall-induced frequency shifts when the sample is placed close to the conducting walls.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework to model the interaction between magnons (spin waves) and photons in a resonant cavity. By employing an advanced Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulation using the electric vector potential, the authors derive canonical polariton variables. This allows for the prediction of key phenomena like mode hybridization and frequency shifts in magnetic polariton systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental physics of magnon-photon interactions within a resonant cavity, aiming to derive a robust theoretical framework for these coupled excitations.
main_result: The authors successfully derive a canonical polariton basis by diagonalizing the coupled system using a generalized Bogoliubov transformation, predicting hybridization and frequency shifts.
method: The methodology involves linearizing coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations, formulating the dynamics via a Lagrangian/Hamiltonian approach using the electric vector potential, and solving the resulting eigenvalue problem.
model_or_system: The system models a ferromagnetic material (e.g., YIG disk) placed inside a microwave cavity, coupling the quantized electromagnetic field (photons) to the collective spin excitations (magnons).
key_observables: Hybrid collective excitations (magnetic polaritons), radiative magnon-photon coupling strength, and cavity-wall-induced frequency shifts.
important_parameters: Gyromagnetic ratio ($\gamma$), exchange stiffness ($A$), anisotropy constant ($K_1$), and the number of retained normal modes ($P$).
main_assumptions: The formulation assumes the use of the electric vector potential to avoid magnetostatic contribution cancellations, and it relies on linearizing the dynamics around a stable micromagnetic ground state.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the geometry of the system, showing the cavity, the magnetic body, and the DC source region.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the fundamental coupled field equations (Maxwell and LL) to developing the advanced Lagrangian/Hamiltonian formulation using the vector potential, deriving the normal modes, and finally applying the formalism to a specific YIG cavity system.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it provides a rigorous, advanced field-theoretic framework (Lagrangian/Hamiltonian/Bogoliubov) to model strong coupling between two distinct quantum systems: cavity photons and magnons.

Color represents the normalized magnitude |H1|/Hmax, and the white streamlines show the direction of H1 at an instant of maximum magnetic amplitude. After half a period all directions reverse, while the field-line pattern and the magnitude are unchanged. The open circle marks the magnetic-field node at the cavity center.

(c) Full magnon–photon spectrum at the same disk position, with the branches n = 1, 6, 15, 16 in black. The horizontal line in (a) and (b) marks the 4 GHz TE101 frequency.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly models the coupling between magnons (spin waves) and cavity photons, leading to the prediction of magnon-photon polaritons, which is a central topic in the spintronics/quantum-optics interface.
